counterevidence_considered.description: The strongest fact favouring the issue class: the input table does contain repeated entries per independent unit (60 rows for 16 gardens, with garden_id repeated 3-4 times), and the code iterates over every one of those rows. However, each row is only appended to its garden's session_gains list and contributes solely to that garden's mean; the repeated rows never enter the t-test as separate observations, so the issue is not realised.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: 60 rows / 16 unique garden_id values; per-row loop feeds within-garden aggregation only

evidence.description: The workflow aggregates repeated visit rows into one value per garden before testing: it builds a list of per-garden mean gains (unit_means) and passes only those 16 unit means to the one-sample t-test, so no repeated row enters the row-independent procedure directly.
evidence.observed_value: ttest_1samp is applied to unit_means (16 garden means), not to the 60 visit rows

evidence.description: The report's degrees of freedom and sample size correspond to the 16 independent gardens (df = 15), not to the 60 visit rows (which would give df = 59), demonstrating that the test statistic was computed at the unit level.
evidence.observed_value: t(15) = 7.714 with n = 16 garden means; row-level analysis would have shown t(59)

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Compost-amended cells infiltrated faster than their paired reference cells by 3.825 mm/h on average (95% CI 2.768 to 4.882 mm/h; two-sided one-sample t-test on 16 garden means, t(15) = 7.714, p < 0.0001).

evidence.description: Independent hand recomputation from data/input.csv reproduces the report exactly: all 16 per-garden mean gains match the report's table (e.g., RG-01 = 3.80, RG-04 = 6.10 from 3 visits, RG-12 = -0.60), and the 16 means yield mean 3.825, SD 1.9834, SE 0.4958, t = 7.714, 95% CI 2.768 to 4.882 — identical to the reported values.

source_refs.quoted_text:
- Mean garden gain: 3.825 mm/h
- SD across gardens: 1.983 mm/h
- Standard error of the mean: 0.496 mm/h
- 95% confidence interval: 2.768 to 4.882 mm/h

evidence.description: The report and the data description agree on the required handling: the description mandates reducing each garden's visits to a single value (16 values for 16 gardens), and the report states that this is exactly what was done, including for the four gardens with only 3 accessible visits.
evidence.observed_value: 16 analysed values for 16 gardens; visit counts 3-4 handled by within-garden averaging

source_refs.quoted_text: Repeated visits to the same garden re-measure the same construction, the same soil profile and the same inlet, so they are not separate independent cases; only the gardens themselves were sited and built independently of one another. An analysis should reduce each garden's visits to a single value before testing, which leaves sixteen values for sixteen gardens. The number of visits is not balanced across gardens, because four sites were inaccessible during the third survey round.

Sessions repeated at the same garden are not independent of one another, so the session gains are averaged within each garden before testing. The reported test therefore uses 16 garden means, one analysed value per independent garden.
The 60 rows are repeated visits rather than 60 independent gardens. The sample size for the reported test is 16 gardens, which fixes the degrees of freedom at 15.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to show the issue was present by testing whether the reported statistics could only arise from feeding the 60 visit rows into the t-test. I recomputed the analysis by hand from data/input.csv both ways. Row-level analysis would give n = 60 and df = 59 with a markedly smaller standard error; the report instead shows n = 16, df = 15, SE = 0.496. Recomputing all 16 per-garden means from the raw rows (including the three-visit gardens RG-04, RG-06, RG-10, RG-14) exactly reproduces the report's per-garden table, and the one-sample t-test on those 16 means reproduces mean 3.825, SD 1.983, SE 0.496, t(15) = 7.714, and CI 2.768 to 4.882 to the reported precision. I also checked the code path for any route by which a raw row could reach stats.ttest_1samp and found none: the only argument is unit_means, built exclusively from per-garden mean_gain values. The falsification attempt failed, confirming the analysis is unit-level.
